children: Indian benchmark indices are likely to open with negative bias on September 17, tracking GIFT Nifty, which was trading lower at around 23,234.50 in early trade.
Track the latest updates on GIFT Nifty right here on Moneycontrol

Indian equity indices bounced back and snapped a two-day losing streak on September 16, with Nifty finishing above 23,200 supported by broad-based buying across sectors, barring IT, while easing oil prices also provided some relief to the market.
At close, the Sensex was up 332.63 points or 0.45 percent at 74,336.45, and the Nifty was up 99.00 points or 0.43 percent at 23,217.60.
Broader markets underperformed the benchmark indices, with the Nifty Midcap 100 index ending flat, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 index closed marginally lower.
Here is how financial markets across the globe fared overnight:
GIFT Nifty (Down)
GIFT Nifty was trading lower at around 23,234.50 in early trade, indicating negative opening for the domestic equity markets.
Asian Equities (Rise)
Asian markets were trading higher in the early trade on THursday.
US Equities (Down)

US stocks whipsawed ​lower on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve raised its key interest rate for the first time in over three years to fight ‌stubbornly high inflation stemming from soaring crude oil prices during the US-Israeli war on Iran.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 631.33 points, or 1.21%, to 51,461.78, the S&P 500 lost 33.59 points, or 0.44%, to 7,552.14 and ‌the Nasdaq ⁠Composite lost 3.15 points, or 0.01%, to 25,978.43.
Dollar Index (Up)
The dollar held onto Wednesday’s gains after the US central bank raised interest rates and signaled more are coming.
The Bloomberg Dollar Spot index stands pat after gaining 0.5% on Wednesday to hit a one-month high.
US Bond Yield (Down)
Treasuries pared losses as Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s resolve to tackle inflation calmed markets following the central bank’s first interest-rate increase since 2023.
The yield on the rate-sensitive two-year US note fell two basis points to 4.72% after climbing to the highest since 2024
in the prior session. Yields on the benchmark 10-year and the 30-year bonds both dropped by two basis points.
Asian Currencies (Mixed)

Asian currencies were mixed against the US dollar in early trade. The Malaysian ringgit declined the most, down 0.57%, followed by the Taiwan dollar (0.30%) and South Korean won (0.25%). The Philippine peso and Thai baht also weakened marginally. Meanwhile, the Indonesian rupiah slipped 0.01%, while the Japanese yen gained 0.10%, China’s renminbi rose 0.05% and the Singapore dollar edged up 0.04%.
Crude (Falls)

Oil prices fell in early trade on Thursday, extending the previous day's losses, as reports of Saudi Arabia offering extra crude cargoes through Oman reduced fears of supply disruptions in the Middle East.

Brent crude futures dropped $1.24, or 1.2%, to $104.59 a barrel by 0049 GMT, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures were down $1.14, or 1.1%, at $101.29. Both contracts fell about $3 on Wednesday.
Gold (Up)

Gold held a decline after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years and signaled another hike was likely before year-end. Bullion was trading around $4,270 an ounce, after falling 2% over the previous three sessions as traders priced in the Fed’s widely expected move.
Fund Flow Action

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) sold equities worth ₹2,000 crore on September 16, while domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continued to provide support, buying equities worth ₹3,900 crore during the session.
